title: Tree DP Maximum Independent Set
problem: In the planning of a new urban district, there is a tree-shaped street network where each plot (node) has a development value. Adjacent plots cannot be developed simultaneously to avoid traffic congestion. Given a tree, where nodes represent plots, value represents development value, and edges represent adjacency. Compute the maximum total development value achievable, returning only the maximum number. The input tree object includes nodes (id, value) and edges (undirected edges).
strategy: dp_take[u] represents the optimal value when u is selected, dp_skip[u] represents the optimal value when u is not selected.
input_contract: Input a tree with value weights.
learning_objectives: Understand the definition and recurrence relationship of dp_take[u] (optimal value when u is selected) and dp_skip[u] (optimal value when u is not selected).
Be able to predict the parent node's state update based on children's dp values.
Observe changes in the global optimal solution by modifying node weights, building an intuitive understanding of state dependencies.

interaction_tasks.feedback_correct: Correct! dp_take only sums children's skip values, dp_skip takes the sum of each child's optimal value.
interaction_tasks.feedback_wrong: Check the formulas: take depends on children's skip, skip depends on each child's optimal value. Recalculate.
interaction_tasks.oracle: Compare predicted (take, skip) with (5+0+0=5, max(3,0)+max(4,0)=7). Allow floating-point error.
interaction_tasks.prompt: Currently traversing node u (id='A'), its value=5, the dp states of its two children B (value=3) and C (value=4) are known: B: take=3, skip=0; C: take=4, skip=0. Predict the dp_take and dp_skip values for node A.
interaction_tasks.stage2_affordance: Highlight node A and its children in the tree view, display relevant values in dp_table, auto-fill predicted results upon click.
